*   $c(s)$ is the initial position of the particle at time $t_0$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that $c(s)$ is the initial position of the particle at time $t_0$. In Source [S1], Definition 3.26 defines the integral surface $S(s, t)$ using the formula $S(s, t) = c(s) + ...$ with the integral starting from $t_0$. By evaluating this equation at $t = t_0$, the integral term becomes zero, resulting in $S(s, t_0) = c(s)$. Since $S(s, t)$ represents the position of a particle at time $t$ seeded at parameter $s$, $c(s)$ represents the position of that particle at the initial time $t_0$. Additionally, the text describes $c(s)$ as a 'seeding curve' from which particles emerge, confirming it defines the starting locations.
